29031-sir-william-herschel-his-life-and-.title: His Life And Works
29031-sir-william-herschel-his-life-and-.creator: Unknown
29031-sir-william-herschel-his-life-and-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Of the great modern philosophers, that one of whom least is known, is WILLIAM HERSCHEL. We may appropriate the words which escaped him when the barren region of the sky near the body of _Scorpio_ was passing slowly through the field of his great reflector, during one of his sweeps, to express our own sense of absence of light and knowledge: _Hier ist wahrhaftig ein Loch im Himmel._

arxiv-2108-10125.title: A Study on Machine Learning Approaches for Player Performance and Match Results Prediction
arxiv-2108-10125.creator: Harsh Mittal, Deepak Rikhari, Jitendra Kumar, Ashutosh Kumar Singh
arxiv-2108-10125.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Harsh Mittal, Deepak Rikhari, Jitendra Kumar, Ashutosh Kumar Singh. Cricket is unarguably one of the most popular sports in the world. Predicting the outcome of a cricket match has become a fundamental problem as we are advancing in the field of machine learning.

arxiv-2203-06081.title: Efficient Bayesian estimation and use of cut posterior in semiparametric hidden Markov models
arxiv-2203-06081.creator: Daniel Moss, Judith Rousseau, Daniel Moss, Judith Rousseau, Daniel Moss, Judith Rousseau, Daniel Moss, Judith Rousseau
arxiv-2203-06081.description: Abstract We consider the problem of estimation in Hidden Markov models with finite state space and nonparametric emission distributions. Efficient estimators for the transition matrix are exhibited, and a semiparametric Bernstein-von Mises result is deduced. Following from this, we propose a modular approach using the cut posterior to jointly estimate the transition matrix and the emission densities.

arxiv-2305-04909.title: On the nature of the planet-powered transient event ZTF SLRN-2020
arxiv-2305-04909.creator: Noam Soker
arxiv-2305-04909.description: Abstract The Red Nova ZTF SLRN-2020 is the third transient event with properties that are compatible with the merger of a planet with a main sequence (or close to) star on a dynamical timescale. While the two first transient events occurred in young stellar objects, ZTF SLRN-2020 occurred in an old system.

arxiv-2401-15856.title: The Indoor-Training Effect : unexpected gains from distribution shifts in the transition function
arxiv-2401-15856.creator: Serena Bono, Spandan Madan, Ishaan Grover Mao Yasueda, Cynthia Breazeal, Hanspeter Pfister, Gabriel Kreiman
arxiv-2401-15856.description: Abstract Is it better to perform tennis training in a pristine indoor environment or a noisy outdoor one? To model this problem, here we investigate whether shifts in the transition probabilities between the training and testing environments in reinforcement learning problems can lead to better performance under certain conditions.

arxiv-2502-04258.title: Detecting Mild Traumatic Brain Injury with MEG Scan Data: One-vs-K-Sample Tests
arxiv-2502-04258.creator: Jian Zhang, 1∗ Gary Green, 2 1 School of Mathematics, Statistics and Actuarial Science, University of Kent, Canterbury, Kent CT2 7NF, UK 2 Department of Psychology, University of York, York YO10 5DD, UK and Innovision IP Ltd, 50 Seymour Street, London W1H 7JG, UK ∗ Correspondence: j.zhang-79@kent.ac
arxiv-2502-04258.description: Abstract Magnetoencephalography (MEG) scanner has been shown to be more accurate than other medical devices in detecting mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI). However, MEG scan data in certain spectrum ranges can be skewed, multimodal and heterogeneous which can mislead the conventional case-control analysis that requires the data to be homogeneous and normally distributed within the control group.

arxiv-2509-23759.title: VioPTT: Violin Technique-Aware Transcription from Synthetic Data Augmentation
arxiv-2509-23759.creator: Ting-Kang Wang, Yueh-Po Peng, Vincent K.M. Cheung
arxiv-2509-23759.description: Abstract While automatic music transcription is well-established in music information retrieval, most models are limited to transcribing pitch and timing information from audio, and thus omit crucial expressive and instrument-specific nuances. One example is playing technique on the violin, which affords its distinct palette of timbres for maximal emotional impact.

britannica-1911-taussig-frank-william.title: Taussig, Frank William (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-taussig-frank-william.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-taussig-frank-william.description: Article 'Taussig, Frank William' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 26), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was born at St Louis, Missouri, on the 28th of December 1859. He was educated in his native city and at Harvard University, where he became professor of political economy in 1892. He has made a particular study of finance, and has written Tariff History of the United States (1888); The Silver Situation in the United States (1892); Wages and Capital (1896).

plos-pone-0008284.creator: Eric Haÿ, Alexandra Nouraud, Pierre J. Marie
plos-pone-0008284.description: PLOS ONE research article. Osteoblasts are bone forming cells that play an essential role in osteogenesis. The elucidation of the mechanisms that control osteoblast number is of major interest for the treatment of skeletal disorders characterized by abnormal bone formation. Canonical Wnt signalling plays a

pmc-12361390.title: Bioengineered hybrid dual-targeting nanoparticles reprogram the tumour microenvironment for deep glioblastoma photodynamic therapy
pmc-12361390.creator: Rongrong Zhao, Ying Hou, Boyan Li, Ziwen Pan, Jiawei Qiu, Qingtong Wang, Yanhua Qi, Zhe Han, Hongyu Zhao, Hong Liu, Weijia Zhou, Gang Li, Hao Xue
pmc-12361390.description: Glioblastoma (GBM) poses significant therapeutic challenges due to its hypoxic and immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME), low immunogenicity and physical barriers. While combining photodynamic therapy (PDT) with immunotherapy holds promise, its efficacy is hampered by insufficient immune activation. In this study, we develop a multifunctional photodynamic-enhanced biomimetic intelligent nanoplatform (FBFO@HM@aOPN) responsive to the TME.

pmc-12374679.title: Neurological outcomes with hypothermia versus normothermia in patients with moderate initial illness severity following resuscitation from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: protocol for a multicentre randomised controlled trial (R-CAST OHCA)
pmc-12374679.creator: Hiromichi Naito, Mitsuaki Nishikimi, Yohei Okada, Hiroki Maeyama, Takeyuki Kiguchi, Takashi Yorifuji, Kazuki Nishida, Shigeyuki Matsui, Yasuhiro Kuroda, Kei Nishiyama, Taku Iwami, Atsunori Nakao, Mitsuaki Nishikimi
pmc-12374679.description: IntroductionTemperature control is a fundamental intervention for neuroprotection following resuscitation from cardiac arrest. However, evidence regarding the efficacy of hypothermia in post-cardiac arrest syndrome (PCAS) remains unclear. Retrospective studies suggest that the clinical effectiveness of hypothermia may depend on the severity of PCAS.

pmc-12950086.title: Optimal designs for discrete-time survival models with competing risks
pmc-12950086.creator: XiaoDong Zhou, YunJuan Wang, RongXian Yue, Weng Kee Wong
pmc-12950086.description: Current methodological research on randomized controlled trial design has predominantly focused on studies with a single primary endpoint. However, many trials in practice involve multiple competing target events. The optimal designs for survival trials with competing target events have not been systematically addressed in the statistical literature.

pmc-12970167.title: Engineering a Glucose‐Responsive Glucagon Prodrug Through Arginine–Phenylboronic Acid Pendant Modification
pmc-12970167.creator: Emily L DeWolf, Weike Chen, Bernice Webber, Elizabeth M Power, Rory Kilmer, Pradeep Kadu, Sijie Xian, Matthew J Webber
pmc-12970167.description: Activatable prodrug strategies offer powerful means to control therapeutic presentation in space and time. Here, we report a single‐molecule prodrug design that enables glucose‐responsive activation of a glucagon analog for hypoglycemia protection. The system conjugates dasiglucagon with a synthetic pendant comprised of alternating arginine and phenylboronic acid (PBA) units, designed to couple peptide solubility to glucose concentration.

pmc-12976653.title: Not Every Country Can Absorb a Shock: Unequal Capacity to Withstand World Health Organization Aid Cuts
pmc-12976653.creator: Animesh Ghimire
pmc-12976653.description: External health aid is contracting sharply, and this moment is often framed as a stress test of health system resilience. This perspective argues that it is equally a stress test of global health ethics and governance: When external actors withdraw from essential services, they are not merely responding to fiscal constraints—they are shaping who loses care.

pmc-12992127.title: Temporal patterns of redisplacement risk following nonoperative treatment of pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-12992127.creator: Jie Zhang, Chaohua Li, Ying Zhao
pmc-12992127.description: Background:Although risk factors for redisplacement after nonoperative treatment of pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures (SCHFs) are well described, the temporal distribution of this risk remains poorly understood. This study investigated temporal patterns of redisplacement and identified independent predictors using time-to-event analysis.

pmc-13201664.title: cGAMP suppresses FTO expression to promote m6A modification and potentiate antitumor immunity
pmc-13201664.creator: Pan Feng, Xiaolan Chen, Dong Guo, Zhihua Feng, Yajuan Fu, Junzhong Lai, Xiaoyu Yang
pmc-13201664.description: Cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP) serves as a pivotal second messenger in the cGAS‒STING innate immune signaling pathway and plays a critical role in antiviral and antitumor immunity; however, its regulatory mechanisms governing the epitranscriptome remain to be elucidated. In this study, m6A methylation sequencing revealed that cGAMP induces dynamic changes in m6A modification in L929 and B16F10 cells.

pmc-13300457.title: The Modifying Effect of Individual-Level Neighborhood Perceptions on the Relationship Between Census-Level Neighborhood Social Vulnerability and Cognition in Older Latinos
pmc-13300457.creator: Melissa Lamar, Cheyenne V. Parson, Crystal M. Glover, Ana W. Capuano, Mayra L. Estrella, Emily P. Morris, Lisa L. Barnes, David A. Bennett, David X. Marquez
pmc-13300457.description: Highlights Public health relevance—How does this work relate to a public health issue? Increasingly, some—but not all—studies suggest residents of highly disadvantaged or vulnerable neighborhoods show lower levels of cognition making neighborhood health a key focus of public health. Public health significance—Why is this work of significance to public health?

pmc-13322387.title: Lost in translation—what is translational neuroscience research?
pmc-13322387.creator: Laurent Sheybani, David Belin
pmc-13322387.description: Our editors discuss and define translational neuroscience research, a concept central to the identity of Brain Communications. Brain Communications was launched in 2019 under the leadership of Professor Tara Spires-Jones, a world expert in the cellular and molecular bases of neurodegenerative disorders, especially Alzheimer’s disease. The ambition was to become home to robust translational neuroscience research.
